children: Effective 2 November, his retirement marks the end of a leadership journey that spanned the company's expansion beyond traditional television distribution.

Harit Nagpal has retired as Managing Director of Tata Play, bringing his 16-year tenure at the television distribution company to an end. His retirement came into effect on 2 November 2026, coinciding with his 65th birthday. However, he will continue to remain associated with the company as a member of its board of directors.

Nagpal joined the company, then known as Tata Sky, in August 2010, succeeding Vikram Kaushik. Over the next 16 years, he led the company's expansion in India's direct-to-home (DTH) television market and its subsequent diversification into broadband and digital content aggregation.

Before joining Tata Sky, Nagpal was Group Marketing Director at Vodafone, where he spent nine years in various leadership roles. His professional journey also includes stints at Shoppers Stop, Pepsi, Marico and Lakmé, giving him experience across consumer goods, retail and telecommunications. He began his career in the packaged goods industry before moving into the services sector.
An alumnus of Panjab University, where he studied chemical engineering, Nagpal also holds an MBA from the Faculty of Management Studies (FMS), University of Delhi.

During his tenure, Tata Play evolved from a DTH-focused service provider into a broader content distribution and entertainment platform. One of the significant milestones was the company's transition from Tata Sky to Tata Play in January 2022, reflecting its expansion beyond satellite television services.

The company had already ventured into broadband and OTT aggregation through Tata Play Binge, which brought multiple streaming services under a single platform. The rebranding was aimed at creating a unified identity for its expanding entertainment and connectivity businesses. At the time, Nagpal said the company's interests had grown beyond DTH services, necessitating a brand identity that reflected its broader ambitions.

More recently, Tata Play expanded its connected television proposition with Tata Play Smart, an internet-based aggregation platform that brings more than 500 live television channels from broadcaster applications onto a single interface.
